You are black-box reverse-engineering a compiled C++ binary at /workspace/dataset/test15_executable.
DO NOT look for or read any C++ library source (there is none on disk anyway).
DO NOT use `strings`, `objdump`, `nm`, `gdb`, or any binary/symbol inspection. Behavioral probing via command-line arguments ONLY.

The binary's driver program is exactly this:

  inflection::Inflector::initialize();
  std::vector<std::string> results;
  for (int i = 1; i < argc && i <= 5; i++) {
      std::string word = argv[i];
      results.push_back(inflection::Inflector::pluralize(word));
      results.push_back(inflection::Inflector::camelize(word));
      if (i % 2 == 0) results.push_back(inflection::Inflector::underscore(word));
  }
  for (const auto& r : results) std::cout << r << std::endl;
  if (argc > 1) {
      std::cout << inflection::Inflector::isPlural(argv[1]) << std::endl;
      std::cout << inflection::Inflector::isSingular(argv[1]) << std::endl;
      std::cout << inflection::Inflector::demodulize("Module::" + std::string(argv[1])) << std::endl;
  }

So to observe a function on an arbitrary word W:
  - pluralize(W)  -> line 1 of `/workspace/dataset/test15_executable "W"`
  - camelize(W)   -> line 2 of `/workspace/dataset/test15_executable "W"`
  - underscore(W) -> `/workspace/dataset/test15_executable dummy "W"` prints: pluralize(dummy), camelize(dummy), pluralize(W), camelize(W), underscore(W), then isPlural/isSingular/demodulize of "dummy". So underscore(W) is line 5.
  - isPlural(W)   -> line 3 of `/workspace/dataset/test15_executable "W"` (prints as 0/1 since it's a bool via operator<<)
  - isSingular(W) -> line 4 of `/workspace/dataset/test15_executable "W"`
  - demodulize("Module::" + W) -> line 5 of `/workspace/dataset/test15_executable "W"`

Run MANY probes (hundreds). Use bash loops. Quote arguments properly. Capture stderr too (2>&1 separately from stdout when it matters) and capture exit codes.
Be systematic: form a hypothesis, then design inputs that DISCRIMINATE between competing hypotheses, then confirm.
Report the exact rule as precise pseudocode operating on BYTES (the C++ code uses std::string = bytes; the "C" locale means std::toupper/tolower only affect ASCII a-z/A-Z). Explicitly test non-ASCII UTF-8 input to confirm byte-level behavior.


=== ADVERSARIAL CROSS-CHECK: pluralize ===

Another engineer probed the `pluralize` behavior of /workspace/dataset/test15_executable and produced this spec. Your job is to FALSIFY it. Assume it is subtly wrong. Design and run inputs specifically engineered to break it, then report every discrepancy between the spec's prediction and the binary's actual output.

SPEC PSEUDOCODE:
// inflection::Inflector::pluralize(const std::string& word) -> std::string
// Pure byte-level operation. No locale/case/UTF-8 awareness whatsoever.

CONST UNCOUNTABLE : set of exact byte strings = {
    "equipment",
    "information",
    "rice",
    "money",
    "species",
    "series",
    "fish",
    "sheep",
    "jeans",
    "police"
}   // exactly 10 entries == Rails' default `uncountables` list, all lowercase ASCII

function pluralize(word):
    if word.size() == 0:
        return ""                      // identity on empty input (NOT "s")
    if UNCOUNTABLE.contains(word):     // EXACT, byte-for-byte, case-SENSITIVE,
        return word                    // whole-string equality. No trimming,
                                       // no lowercasing, no substring or
                                       // word-boundary scan, no suffix stripping.
    return word + "s"                  // append the single byte 0x73 ('s')

// Equivalent one-liner:
//   result = (word.empty() || UNCOUNTABLE.count(word)) ? word : word + 's';
//
// NON-BEHAVIORS (all explicitly verified):
//  * There are NO other rules at all. No -es for s/ss/sh/ch/x/z endings,
//    no y->ies, no f/fe->ves, no o->oes, no is->es, no us->i, no um->a,
//    no on->a, no ix/ex->ices, and NO irregular table (man/woman/child/
//    person/tooth/foot/goose/mouse/louse/ox/die/penny/quiz/datum/index/
//    matrix/appendix/criterion/...). Every one gains a trailing 's'.
//  * Uncountables NOT in the set despite being plausible: news, water, data,
//    staff, advice, music, luggage, furniture, bison, salmon, trout, swine,
//    aircraft, offspring, deer, moose, buffalo, corps, means, scissors,
//    pants, shoes, clothes, glasses, chinese, japanese, mathematics, physics,
//    software, homework, research, evidence, feedback, traffic, weather,
//    cattle, people, gold, milk, cash, ... (263 candidates swept; only the
//    10 listed above were unchanged).
//  * Bytes are never inspected or transformed other than the append. Any byte
//    0x01..0xFF in any position (incl. invalid UTF-8 such as 0xFF, 0x80,
//    0xC0 0xAF) passes through unchanged with 0x73 appended.
//  * Length is unbounded (verified 100000-byte input -> 100001 bytes).
//  * Never throws; exit code 0; nothing on stderr.
//    (The only crash in this binary comes from demodulize("Module::") when
//     argv[1] is empty -- pluralize itself already produced "" successfully.)

CLAIMED FINDINGS:
1. COMPLETE RULE: pluralize(w) = w.empty() ? w : (UNCOUNTABLE.count(w) ? w : w + "s"). Nothing else exists.
2. The uncountable set is EXACTLY the 10-word Rails default list: equipment, information, rice, money, species, series, fish, sheep, jeans, police. Swept 263 distinct mass-noun / -ese-nationality / pluralia-tantum / Latin-plural candidates; only those 10 were returned unchanged.
3. Explicitly ruled out as uncountable (each got +s): news->newss, water, data, staff, advice, music, luggage, furniture, bison, salmon, trout, swine, aircraft, offspring, deer->deers, moose->mooses, buffalo->buffalos, corps->corpss, means->meanss, scissors->scissorss, pants->pantss, shoes->shoess, clothes->clothess, glasses->glassess, chinese->chineses, japanese->japaneses, portuguese, swiss->swisss, mathematics, physics, politics, economics, mumps, measles, molasses, cattle, poultry, people, software, hardware, homework, housework, research->researchs, evidence, feedback, traffic, weather, mail, email, cash->cashs, currency, gold, silver, sand, wheat, flour, butter, cheese, milk, coffee, tea, beer, wine, bread, meat, chicken, beef, pork, sugar, salt, pepper, oil, gas->gass, electricity, energy, power, knowledge, wisdom, happiness->happinesss, sadness, anger, fear, hope, faith, trust, honesty, courage, patience, kindness->kindnesss, metadata, media, info, crossroads, headquarters, spacecraft, elk, cod, carp, squid, shrimp.
4. LOOKUP IS CASE-SENSITIVE (raw byte compare, no lowercasing, no case-preserving restore). Fish->Fishs, FISH->FISHs, fIsh->fIshs, fisH->fisHs, Money->Moneys, MONEY->MONEYs, Series->Seriess, SERIES->SERIESs, Police->Polices, POLICE->POLICEs, Jeans->Jeanss, JEANS->JEANSs, Equipment->Equipments, EQUIPMENT->EQUIPMENTs, Information->Informations, Rice->Rices, RICE->RICEs, Species->Speciess, SPECIES->SPECIESs, Sheep->Sheeps, SHEEP->SHEEPs, MoNeY->MoNeYs. Only the all-lowercase forms match.
5. WHOLE-STRING MATCH ONLY, no trimming, no word-boundary logic: fishing->fishings, fishes->fishess, myfish->myfishs, goldfish->goldfishs, "fish "->"fish s", " fish"->" fishs", "big fish"->"big fishs", fish_bowl->fish_bowls, moneybag->moneybags, policeman->policemans, seriesX->seriesXs, "series."->"series.s", "fish-"->"fish-s", "-fish"->"-fishs", "police!"->"police!s", money2->money2s, "	fish"->"	fishs", "fish	"->"fish	s", " Fish"->" Fishs".
6. NO SUFFIX RULES WHATSOEVER. Verified +s on: bus->buss, glass->glasss, wish->wishs, church->churchs, box->boxs, buzz->buzzs, quiz->quizs, baby->babys, city->citys, boy->boys, potato->potatos, hero->heros, echo->echos, photo->photos, piano->pianos, leaf->leafs, life->lifes, knife->knifes, wife->wifes, wolf->wolfs, calf->calfs, thief->thiefs, loaf->loafs, self->selfs, elf->elfs, hoof->hoofs, roof->roofs, belief->beliefs, chief->chiefs, chef->chefs, safe->safes, giraffe->giraffes.
7. NO IRREGULAR TABLE. man->mans, woman->womans, child->childs, person->persons, tooth->tooths, foot->foots, goose->gooses, mouse->mouses, louse->louses, ox->oxs, die->dies, penny->pennys, analysis->analysiss, crisis->crisiss, thesis->thesiss, cactus->cactuss, focus->focuss, radius->radiuss, alumnus->alumnuss, syllabus->syllabuss, status->statuss, virus->viruss, bonus->bonuss, criterion->criterions, phenomenon->phenomenons, datum->datums, medium->mediums, curriculum->curriculums, index->indexs, matrix->matrixs, vertex->vertexs, appendix->appendixs, oxen->oxens, house->houses, boot->boots, booth->booths.
8. EMPTY STRING IS IDENTITY: pluralize("") == "" (NOT "s"). Confirmed twice: as argv[1] (line 1 blank, before the unrelated demodulize abort) and as argv[2] (line 3 blank, exit 0).
9. EXHAUSTIVE SINGLE-BYTE SWEEP: every byte value 0x01..0xFF used as a 1-byte word produced exactly that byte followed by 0x73. Zero deviations across all 254 tested (0x0A included separately: "
" -> "
s", hex 0a 73). 0x00 is untestable through argv.
10. BYTE-LEVEL, NOT UTF-8 AWARE: caf\xC3\xA9 -> 63 61 66 C3 A9 73; na\xC3\xAFve -> ...73; \xE6\x97\xA5\xE6\x9C\xAC\xE8\xAA\x9E -> e697a5 e69cac e8aa9e 73; \xCE\xA9 -> cea9 73; U+FB01 \xEF\xAC\x81sh (‘ﬁsh’) -> efac81 73 68 73 (i.e. NOT normalized to "fish", so no Unicode folding before the uncountable lookup); fullwidth ＦＩＳＨ -> +73. Invalid UTF-8 preserved: 0xFF -> ff73, 0x80 -> 8073, 0xC0 0xAF -> c0af73, 0xFF 0xFE -> fffe73, "fish\xFF" -> 66697368ff73, "\xFFfish" -> ff6669736873.
11. WHITESPACE-ONLY: " " -> " s"; "  " -> "  s"; "	" -> "	s"; "		" -> "		s"; "
" -> "
s"; "  a  " -> "  a  s". Embedded control chars pass through: "a	b"->"a	bs", "a
b"->"a
bs", "a b"->"a bs".
12. LONG STRINGS: 5000 'a' -> 5001 bytes ending "aas"; 1250x"fish" (5000 bytes) -> 5001 bytes ending "hfishs"; 100000 'x' -> 100001 bytes ending "xxs". Linear, no truncation, no length special case.
13. BULK NEGATIVE CONTROL: 268 curated English words plus 300 random ASCII strings (letters/digits/space/._-) all returned exactly input+"s" -- zero deviations. Total probes across this dimension ~1100+.
14. No stderr output and exit code 0 for every non-empty argv[1]; pluralize never throws.

CLAIMED UNCERTAINTIES:
Whether the empty-string identity comes from an explicit `if (word.empty()) return word;` guard or from "" being a member of the uncountable container is not observable black-box; the behavior is identical either way.
The container type (std::set vs unordered_set vs vector+std::find) is unobservable; only exact-byte whole-string membership semantics were confirmed.
Whether Inflector::initialize() could register a different uncountable set under other conditions is untestable through this driver; the observed set is fixed at those 10 words.
A NUL byte (0x00) inside the word cannot be passed via argv, so that byte value is untested (all of 0x01-0xFF were tested and behave as plain bytes).
Only lengths up to 100000 bytes were probed; no allocation-failure path was exercised.

  out=$(./test15_executable "x" "$w" 2>/dev/null | sed -n '3p')
  if [ "$out" != "${w}s" ]; then
    printf 'DEVIATION: input=[%s] -> [%s]\n' "$w" "$out"
  fi
done
EOF

cd /workspace/dataset; fail=0
for i in $(seq 1 255); do
  h=$(printf '%02x' $i)
  b=$(printf "\\x$h")
  # skip newline for this test (handled separately)
  if [ "$i" = "10" ]; then continue; fi
  out=$(./test15_executable "$b" 2>/dev/null | head -1 | xxd -p | tr -d '\n')
  exp="${h}73"
  # xxd of head -1 includes trailing newline 0a
  exp="${h}730a"
  if [ "$out" != "$exp" ]; then printf 'DEV byte %s -> %s (exp %s)\n' "$h" "$out" "$exp"; fail=1; fi
done
echo "singlebyte sweep done fail=$fail"

cd /workspace/dataset; cat > /tmp/batch.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# stdin: words, one per line (no newlines/empty). batches 5 per exec.
lines=(1 3 6 8 11)
buf=()
flush() {
  n=${#buf[@]}
  [ $n -eq 0 ] && return
  mapfile -t out < <(./test15_executable "${buf[@]}" 2>/dev/null)
  for ((k=0;k<n;k++)); do
    idx=${lines[$k]}
    got="${out[$((idx-1))]}"
    exp="${buf[$k]}s"
    [ "$got" = "$exp" ] || printf 'DEV [%s] -> [%s]\n' "${buf[$k]}" "$got"
  done
  buf=()
}
while IFS= read -r w; do
  [ -z "$w" ] && continue
  buf+=("$w")
  [ ${#buf[@]} -eq 5 ] && flush
done
flush
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/batch.sh
